title: Mixing Time Matters: Accelerating Effective Resistance Estimation via Bidirectional Method

problem.claim: Efficiently approximate the effective resistance between two nodes in an undirected graph with small absolute error ε.

gap.claim: The previous best algorithm has worst-case complexity Õ(Lmax^3/ε^2d^2).

contributions.claim: Improve the effective-resistance estimation complexity to Õ(min(Lmax^(7/3)/ε^(2/3), Lmax^3/(ε^2d^2), mLmax)).
Achieve the stated theoretical improvement over previous results.
Report experiments on real-world and synthetic graph datasets comparing the method with baseline methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report a 10× to 1000× running-time speedup while maintaining the same absolute error as baseline methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies efficient effective-resistance approximation on undirected graphs.
The prior best algorithm has complexity depending on mixing time, error, and endpoint degrees.
The paper presents improved complexity bounds and quantifies the theoretical improvement.
The improvement is described as especially significant when mixing time is large in real-world networks.
Experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets report substantial speedups at the same absolute error.

source_observation.claim: The reported complexity improvement is especially relevant when the graph's mixing-time-dependent quantity Lmax is large.

interpretation.claim: Algorithmic improvements should be evaluated against the parameter regimes that dominate practical cost.

application.claim: When optimizing graph algorithms, target bottleneck parameters that are large in the intended deployment networks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the improvement is equally important for graphs with small Lmax.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the bidirectional method's algorithmic steps.
The abstract does not identify the experimental datasets, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide proof details for the stated complexity bounds.
